subject: Recap & Action: Prompt edge-cases collection for legal summarization pilot
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rios <maya@clearpath.ai>, Carl Huang <carl.h@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & Action: Prompt edge-cases collection for legal summarization pilot

Hi Maya / Carl —

Great conversation today — appreciate you walking us through the Clearpath summarization use case and the sample transcripts. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) What we heard (short):
- Primary need: accurate, redaction-safe legal summarization for client transcripts and mixed doc types (emails, meeting notes, exhibits).
- Priority edge cases: PII/PHI spread across documents, inline legal citations, OCR artifacts, and very long nested threads.
- Success metrics: 95% redaction recall for PII; summary factuality within 2% error rate on our benchmark set.

2) Recommended evaluation approach (initial):
- Model shortlist: rw-instruct-large-quant (fast, cost-efficient), redwood-phi-1 (higher safety/PII handling).
- Benchmarks: we will run a lightweight 500-prompt pass focusing on redaction and citation preservation. Results will be shared as CSV + sample diffs.

3) Asks from Clearpath (action items):
- Can you upload a representative set of customer prompts and edge-case examples (redacted or synthetic) to the secure Drive folder we shared? Suggested format: one example per row with columns: prompt, source_type (email/transcript), PII_present (yes/no), expected_redaction (text).
- Any internal redaction policies or must-keep fields we should know about (e.g., token retention rules for court IDs)?

4) Next milestones & owners: 
- Alex: kickoff evaluation, produce baseline benchmarks (EOD 1/22).
- Karthik: set up model configs and safety filters; coordinate run.
- Maya / Carl: upload prompt examples + any redaction guidance to Drive by 1/20.

Attachments: I attached a small sample CSV with the column layout we prefer (clearpath_prompt_examples.csv) and a short redaction guidance template (redaction_guidance.pdf) to make uploads easier.

If that looks right, please reply with confirmation and a note if any of the milestones/timelines need moving. We'll schedule a quick sync on Wednesday next week to review the baseline results.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

----
Attachment: clearpath_prompt_examples.csv (CSV, 5KB)
Attachment: redaction_guidance.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Maya Rios <maya@clearpath.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Carl Huang <carl.h@clearpath.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & Action: Prompt edge-cases collection for legal summarization pilot

Thanks Alex — this is perfect and captures everything we discussed. Quick clarifications from our side before we upload: 

- We will provide three categories of examples: (A) redacted real transcripts (we’ll replace names with <NAME>), (B) synthetic examples that reproduce tricky inline citations, and (C) OCR-noise samples (scanned exhibits).
- Redaction policy: we must remove social security numbers and full client IDs, but partial case numbers (first 4 digits) can remain. I attached our short internal note (redaction_guidance.pdf) — it lists fields that must be redacted vs. fields that can be preserved for context.
- Edge cases to highlight in the CSV: nested quoted emails inside transcripts, timestamps embedded in free text, and legal citation chains (e.g., \"Smith v. Jones, 2012\"). Those are likely to break naive redactors.

We'll upload: clearpath_prompt_upload_v1.zip (contains CSV + sample docs) to the Drive link by COB 1/20. One ask: for any files containing masked sensitive tokens, please confirm how Redwood will handle KV caching and whether masked tokens are excluded from logging for the evaluation runs. If needed, we can provide a short NDA addendum for the evaluation storage.

Best,
Maya Rios
Head of Product, Clearpath Analytics
maya@clearpath.ai | 415-867-4021

----
Attachment: clearpath_prompt_upload_v1.zip (ZIP, 1.2MB)
Attachment: redaction_guidance.pdf (PDF, 12KB)

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rios <maya@clearpath.ai>, Carl Huang <carl.h@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & Action: Prompt edge-cases collection for legal summarization pilot

Hi Maya — thanks for the clarifications and for committing to the upload. Two quick notes on the technical side so you can share with your security/compliance folks: 

- KV caching/logging: for the evaluation we will run on a dedicated, ephemeral evaluation pool; masked tokens in uploaded artifacts will not be stored in persistent caches. We will also enable request-level redaction to strip fields marked as PII per your guidance. I’ll have Karthik send a short technical note with config flags.
- Recommended model/ops baseline: we suggest running a baseline comparison between redwood-phi-1 (safety-first) and rw-instruct-large-quant (cost baseline), with our standard safety filters enabled. For any client-facing scoring we’ll compute: redaction_recall, redaction_precision, summary_factuality (human-annotated), and latency P95.

Attached: benchmark_results_v1.csv is a short sample from a similar pilot (anonymized) so you can see output format. Our plan: run the 500-prompt pass on Thursday (1/22) and share a detailed results CSV + sample diffs by EOD that day.

Action items update: 
- Maya/Carl: upload by 1/20 (you flagged 1/20 — thank you).
- Karthik: send technical note and eval config (by 1/21).
- Alex: run eval and share results (by 1/22).

Laura — tagging you in case we need to expedite any procurement/entitlements for the dedicated ephemeral pool.

Cheers,
Alex

----
Attachment: benchmark_results_v1.csv (CSV, 22KB)
